title: Adjustment Disorder - BSV and Vocal Signals
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: BSV / Vocal

BSV / VOCAL SIGNALS: Typically acute rise in Arousal (restlessness, sleep disruption, tension) and drop in Valence (sadness, irritability, worry) temporally linked to the stressor. Dominance may be reduced (feeling overwhelmed or helpless). Voice often shows increased tension, sighing, or breathiness during discussion of the stressor. Prosody may normalize when talking about unrelated topics.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "I feel on edge all the time since it happened", "My voice cracks when I talk about the divorce".

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: Chronic low valence without clear temporal link to recent stressor argues against adjustment disorder. Persistent high arousal without stressor context suggests GAD or PTSD.

PROVENANCE: Observational studies of stress reactivity. Voice analysis literature on acute vs chronic distress prosody.
